meta.title: HAZOP and LOPA of the P-200 unit
meta.scope: From the tank-farm transfer (HIC-199) into T200, through V200, strainer S-200 and the common suction header, the two pump legs P-200A and P-200B (suction valves, pumps and motors, check valves NRV-210/220, discharge valves V201/V205), the discharge header with FE-100 and V100 (FRC-100), preheater E-100 with TV-110 on LP steam, to the cat-cracker feed drum D-150; utilities: LP steam, instrument air, power (MCC).
meta.objective: Identify the hazards and operability problems of the unit, judge their risk, and decide what must be added or changed. For the scenarios that need more than the existing safeguards, check the risk reduction by LOPA.
meta.assump: Design case: gas oil at 60 °C, 14 L/s with pump A running and B lined up as the spare, feed heated to 150 °C, D-150 at about 50 %. Trained operators. Risk matrix and target event frequencies are those of the OTS HAZOP and LOPA tabs (teaching values).
meta.protocol: Method: HAZOP to IEC 61882 with full recording. The team takes one node at a time, states its design intent, and applies the guide words to each parameter to find deviations. For each deviation it records the causes, the events that follow, the consequences without credit for safeguards, the existing safeguards, and the risk after safeguards (S × L). Rows above the tolerable level go to LOPA in the same worksheet: initiating-event frequency, enabling conditions and conditional modifiers, independent protection layers with their PFD, and the mitigated frequency compared with the tolerable event likelihood for the severity. Open points go to the Parking Lot; actions become recommendations with an owner and a due date.

N3.causes:
Motor A trips (protection relay, fault library)
power dip
single-phasing trips the overload
N3.cons: Feed to the cat cracker lost; D-150 empties and the cat cracker trips its charge pump; with the steam still on, the oil standing in E-100 heats toward the steam temperature.

N3.dev: Pump running against a blocked discharge (deadhead)
N3.causes:
V201 closed in the field by mistake (fault library)
V100 closed by air failure, ESD or LSHH-150
N3.cons: All motor power goes into the casing liquid (about 6 °C per minute): seal faces flash, the seal fails, hot gas oil is released; prolonged deadhead can damage the casing.
N3.notes:
Worked example
LOPA (worked example): values from the OTS LOPA tab, scenario L1 (deadheaded pump), for the cause "discharge block valve closed in the field" only. Credited: TSHH-212 → motor A tripped (PFD 0.007). Not credited: the TI-212 HI alarm, because it shares TE-212 with the trip. Conditional modifier: probability of ignition 0.1. f_mit = 0.1 × 0.1 × 0.007 = 7.00e-05 per year against TEL 0.001 for S4. The other causes of L1 (instrument-air failure, the cat cracker stopping) are worked on the OTS LOPA tab.

ie.d: Discharge block valve of the running pump closed in the field (wrong valve, work permit) (OTS LOPA tab, scenario L1; Assumed (human error))

cm.d: Probability of ignition of the released gas oil (Assumed (gas oil above its flash point, below autoignition))

N3.dev: Pump delivers less than its curve
N3.causes:
Wear rings worn (fault library)
impeller damage
V201 disc parted from its stem (fault library)
N3.cons: FRC-100 opens V100 to the limit and the feed is still short; at low flow the pump runs rough and hot.

N3.causes: Two supply phases swapped after electrical work (fault library)
N3.cons: About 60 % of the head and far less flow; the impeller nut can work loose on reverse rotation and wreck the pump.

N3.causes:
Single-phasing (fault library)
running out at high flow in parallel with V100 wide open
mechanical binding
N3.cons: Motor windings overheat: insulation damage, motor fire.

N3.causes:
Casing not vented before the start (air lock)
suction valve closed
loss of prime
N3.cons: Seal faces run dry and fail within about a minute (model): gas oil sprays from the seal, fire.

N3.causes: Discharge blocked (V100 or V201 closed) with the pump running
N3.cons: The header rises to the shut-off head plus the suction head; above the piping rating only if the rating was set for the operating point.

N3.causes: Worn or damaged mechanical seal after cavitation, dry running or vibration
N3.cons: Gas oil at 60 °C sprays or pools under the pump; ignition on the hot motor or coupling gives a pool fire that can spread to the spare.

N3.dev: No remote view of the pump head
N3.causes:
PI-210 is a local gauge
II-210 is the only remote pump signal
N3.cons: Loss of head, wear or reverse rotation is seen late, from the flow and the valve position only.

Spare pump lined up for a manual start

Overload relay 49-210: > 21.7 A for 10 s → motor A tripped
Start permissives: SIS reset, T200 ≥ 15 %, no motor trip latched, suction valve open and casing vented (both confirmed in the field)
Seal-leak alarm (gas detector at each pump)

recs.text: Auto-start of the spare pump on loss of the running pump (motor trip or low header pressure), with the zero-speed permissive of R15.
Steam cut-off: close TV-110 automatically when the feed flow is lost (FT-100 low or both pumps stopped).
Minimum-flow recycle from each pump discharge (upstream of the check valve) back to T200, sized for the API 610 minimum continuous flow.
Low-flow trip of the running pump (flow in each pump leg, or FT-100 low with V100 closed, time-delayed) so a blocked discharge stops the motor before the casing gets hot.
Header pressure transmitter PIT-100 upstream of FE-100/V100 with a high alarm (blocked outlet, pump at shut-off) and a low alarm (pump lost).
Pump condition monitoring: performance test against the curve every quarter, wear-ring clearances at overhaul.
FRC-100 output-high alarm (V100 above 95 % = loop saturated) and a high clamp on the remote set point.
Rotation (bump) test and phase-sequence check in the close-out of any electrical work on the pump motors.
Dry-run protection: under-power relay on each motor, and a vent sight glass to prove the casing is liquid-full before a start.
Remotely operated, fire-safe emergency isolation valve EIV-200 on the T200 outlet, closable from the control room.
Dual mechanical seals (API 682) with seal-leak detection; seal drip pans with a kerb to the oily-water sewer.
Casing pressure transmitters PIT-210/220 with a high alarm on the idle pump (Rev C option on the SIS tab).
Vibration transmitters on P-200A/B with DCS alarms (VI-210/220 are local today).
